questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Sum of a Geometric Series by Determining the Common Ratio
questions.problem: Determine the value of the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{4}\frac{1}{{6}^{n}}$  rounded to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that we can rewrite the series as follows:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{4}\frac{1}{{6}^{n}}={\sum }_{n=1}^{4}{(\frac{1}{6})}^{n}
$$

Since the above series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}a{r}^{n},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $r=\frac{1}{6}$ and $N=4.$ We need to figure out ${a}_{1}.$

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
{a}_{n}={(\frac{1}{6})}^{n},
$$

and therefore the first term of the series is

$$
{a}_{1}={(\frac{1}{6})}^{1}=\frac{1}{6}.
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=\frac{1}{6},r=\frac{1}{6}$ and $N=4$ into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{4}{(\frac{1}{6})}^{n} & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot \frac{[1-{(\frac{1}{6})}^{4}]}{(1-\frac{1}{6})} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot [1-{(\frac{1}{6})}^{4}] \\  & ≈0.200\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the final answer has been rounded to three decimal places.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Sum of a Simplified Geometric Series Given in Sigma Notation
questions.worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}a{r}^{n},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $r=3$ and $N=8.$ We need to figure out the value of ${a}_{1}.$

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
{a}_{n}=2(3)^{n},
$$

and therefore we can calculate the first term ${a}_{1}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =2(3)^{1} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=6,r=3$ and $N=8$ into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{8}2(3)^{n} & =6\cdot \frac{(1-{3}^{8})}{1-3} \\  & =6\cdot \frac{(-6\,560)}{(-2)} \\  & =6(3\,280) \\  & =19\,680\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Sum of a Geometric Series by Determining the Common Ratio
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that we can rewrite the series as follows:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{4}\frac{12}{{8}^{n}}={\sum }_{n=1}^{4}12\cdot {(\frac{1}{8})}^{n}
$$

Since the above series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}a{r}^{n},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $r=\frac{1}{8}$ and $N=4.$ We need to figure out ${a}_{1}.$

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
{a}_{n}=12\cdot {(\frac{1}{8})}^{n},
$$

and therefore the first term of the series is

$$
{a}_{1}=12\cdot {(\frac{1}{8})}^{1}=\frac{3}{2}.
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=\frac{3}{2},r=\frac{1}{8}$ and $N=4$ into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{5}12\cdot {(\frac{1}{8})}^{n} & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{[1-{(\frac{1}{8})}^{4}]}{(1-\frac{1}{8})} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{(1-\frac{1}{4096})}{\frac{7}{8}} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{8}{7}\cdot \frac{4095}{4096} \\  & =\frac{1755}{1024}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $r=\frac{1}{4}$ and $N=4.$ We need to figure out the value of ${a}_{1}.$

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
{a}_{n}=10{(\frac{1}{4})}^{n},
$$

and therefore, we can calculate the first term ${a}_{1}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =10{(\frac{1}{4})}^{1} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=\frac{5}{2},r=\frac{1}{4}$ and $N=4$ into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{4}10{(\frac{1}{4})}^{n} & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{(1-{(\frac{1}{4})}^{4})}{(1-\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{(1-\frac{1}{256})}{(\frac{3}{4})} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{(\frac{255}{256})}{(\frac{3}{4})} \\  & =\frac{425}{128}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Sum of a Geometric Series Given With a Zero Starting Index
questions.worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form $\sum a{r}^{n-1},$ it is a geometric series. Notice that the index starts from $n=0$ instead of $n=1.$

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{0}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $r=6.$ Also, note that $N=4,$ since there are $4$ terms in total.

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{1}{3}{(6)}^{n-1},
$$

and so the first term ${a}_{0}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{1}{3}{(6)}^{0-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{(6)}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{0}=\frac{1}{18},r=6$ and $N=4$ into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{4} & =\frac{1}{18}\cdot \frac{(1-{6}^{4})}{(1-6)} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}\cdot \frac{(1-1296)}{(-5)} \\  & =\frac{1295}{90} \\  & =\frac{259}{18}\end{aligned}
$$
